protocol.comparison: same DeBERTa scores and Rashomon candidates; only Tableau context changes

interpretation.rashomon_effect: positive candidate-retention effect remains +26pp over DeBERTa Top-1
interpretation.tableau_effect: none observed under either path-only or ontology-relevant local-subgraph context
interpretation.dataset_diagnosis: WN18RR supplies mostly positive lexical relation triples and only limited hard ontology constraints. The candidate worlds rarely violate the configured symmetry/transitivity/irreflexivity/antisymmetry rules, so Tableau has little opportunity to prune.
interpretation.decision: Use WN18RR primarily for multi-hop relation scoring and Rashomon retention. Evaluate Tableau contribution on an ontology-rich dataset with explicit incompatibility/disjointness/negative constraints such as UMLS-derived ontology rules, or on a controlled contradiction-injection ablation.
